newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-NEW ZEALAND BEAT BRITAIN TO ENSURE SERIES WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-NEW ZEALAND BEAT BRITAIN TO ENSURE SERIES WIN.

text.p: New Zealand came from behind for the second match running to upstage Britain 18-15 on Friday to ensure their first rugby league test series victory over their rivals since 1984.
Stand-off Gene Ngamu cut through the British defence 15 minutes from the end to score in the right-hand corner for the decisive try, which New Zealand captain Matthew Ridge converted.

But the outcome was in doubt until the final whistle, with replacement New Zealand back Marc Ellis outsprinting three British players to pick up a loose ball in his in-goal and thwart what would have been a match-winning try.

"The guys dug deep in the second half and we hung in there right to the end and pinched the result in the last 10 or 15 minutes," Ridge said after his side secured only their second ever series victory over Britain.
"We showed a lot of character and spirt. If we put it together for 80 minutes, we will be right up there in world rugby."
The home side dominated a tense opening that featured an early scuffle between Ridge and British scrum-half Bobbie Goulding.
Ridge opened the scoring with a penalty in the 18th minute, taking his test points tally to 134 and overhauling Des White's New Zealand record of 132.

Britain responded quickly with Denis Betts splitting the Kiwi defence and passing for winger Alan Hunte to score the opening try. Goulding converted and then added a drop goal from 20 metres to open a 7-2 lead.
Both sides added a converted try before the break through New Zealand's Reuben Wiki and Britain's Betts.
Wiki scored the try of the match with a 60-metre burst to cut the deficit to a point, but Goulding's penalty stretched the British lead to 15-12.
As in last week's first test in Auckland when the home side ran in two late tries for a 17-12 victory, New Zealand finished strongly and Ngamu's try sealed the outcome.
New Zealand now have a chance of achieving a 3-0 whitewash in next week's final test in Christchurch.
New Zealand - Matthew Ridge, Sean Hoppe, Ruben Wiki, John Timu, Richard Barnett, Gene Ngamu, Stacey Jones; Tyran Smith, Stephen Kearney, Tony Iro, Grant Young, Syd Eru, Quentin Pongia.

Britain - Stuart Spruce, Alan Hunte, Kris Radlinski, Daryl Powell, Anthony Sullivan, Iestyn Harris, Bobbie Goulding; Andy Farrell, Paul Sculthorpe, Denis Betts, Terry O'Connor, Keiron Cunningham, Paul Broadbent.
